faq_heading: Vancouver market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Vancouver in 2 parts: Vancouver East and Vancouver West. In September 2026, Vancouver West had the highest all-home benchmark at $1,206,600 and Vancouver East the lowest at $1,120,200, a gap of $86,400. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Vancouver East down 5.0%, Vancouver West down 5.3%.
Vancouver East benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical Vancouver East home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,120,200 in September 2026. That is up 0.7% on the month, down 1.4% over three months, down 3.5% over six months and down 5.0% over the year. Over three years it is down 8.8%, and over five years up 1.0%.
The weakest one-year move in Vancouver East was for a townhouse homes at −7.9%; the strongest was an apartment at −5.2%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,630,500) and an apartment ($634,800) is $995,700, and a townhouse ($980,400) sits $345,600 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,075,900, Vancouver East is 4.1% above. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.5% against down 5.0% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Vancouver East ranks 6 by all-home benchmark, with Vancouver West above it at $1,206,600 and Tsawwassen below it at $1,113,100.

Detached homes in Vancouver East: benchmark $1,630,500, up 0.6% in a month, down 1.8% in three months, down 4.1% in six months, down 7.7% in a year, down 13.9% in three years and down 3.6% in five. That is 8.6% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,784,700).

Townhouse homes in Vancouver East: benchmark $980,400, down 0.5% in a month, down 7.1% in three months, down 6.1% in six months, down 7.9% in a year, down 13.1% in three years and down 4.1% in five. That is 3.6% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,016,700).

Apartment homes in Vancouver East: benchmark $634,800, up 1.0% in a month, down 0.4% in three months, down 5.2% in six months, down 5.2% in a year, down 11.1% in three years and down 1.3% in five. That is 7.0% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($682,500).

blocks.text: Vancouver West benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical Vancouver West home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,206,600 in September 2026. That is down 1.3% on the month, down 2.7% over three months, down 0.7% over six months and down 5.3% over the year. Over three years it is down 9.6%, and over five years down 5.8%.
The weakest one-year move in Vancouver West was for a detached home homes at −8.7%; the strongest was an apartment at −5.2%.
The gap between a detached home ($2,916,100) and an apartment ($761,800) is $2,154,300, and a townhouse ($1,298,500) sits $536,700 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,075,900, Vancouver West is 12.1% above. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.5% against down 5.3% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Vancouver West ranks 5 by all-home benchmark, with North Vancouver above it at $1,290,400 and Vancouver East below it at $1,120,200.

Detached homes in Vancouver West: benchmark $2,916,100, down 0.6% in a month, down 4.1% in three months, down 0.3% in six months, down 8.7% in a year, down 16.4% in three years and down 12.0% in five. That is 63.4% above the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,784,700).

Townhouse homes in Vancouver West: benchmark $1,298,500, down 2.7% in a month, down 3.9% in three months, down 7.1% in six months, down 5.5% in a year, down 8.4% in three years and down 2.4% in five. That is 27.7% above the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,016,700).

Apartment homes in Vancouver West: benchmark $761,800, down 1.7% in a month, down 2.2% in three months, down 2.2% in six months, down 5.2% in a year, down 9.8% in three years and down 3.6% in five. That is 11.6% above the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($682,500).

blocks.text: What the Vancouver figure is
The $1,120,200 Vancouver East figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for September 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Vancouver?
faq.a: In September 2026, a typical Vancouver East home was $1,120,200, with detached at $1,630,500. In September 2026, a typical Vancouver West home was $1,206,600, with detached at $2,916,100.

faq.q: Are Vancouver home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Vancouver East is down 5.0% over twelve months and down 1.4% over three months. Vancouver West is down 5.3% over twelve months and down 2.7% over three months.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.
